title: Thermodynamic Spectroscopy of Emergent Excitations in Quantum Spin Ice
authors: Zhengbang Zhou, Tony An, Yong Baek Kim
abstract: Quantum spin ice (QSI) is a three-dimensional quantum spin liquid where fractionalized spinons interact with emergent photons. The XXZ model on the pyrochlore lattice realizes such a $U(1)$ quantum spin liquid and a number of pyrochlore magnets have been investigated as candidate materials, but the detection of emergent excitations has been a major challenge. The specific heat is expected to show the higher-energy spinon excitations and a lower-energy anomaly at the ring-exchange scale, which sets both the photon bandwidth and the energy of the emergent magnetic monopoles (or visons). In reality, the lower-energy peak is obscured by the nuclear Schottky anomaly in non-Kramers Pr-based systems, while it is not clearly resolved from the spinon contributions in Ce-based dipolar-octupolar systems. In this work, we propose a novel thermodynamic probe of the elusive ring-exchange energy scale. We show that in the presence of a weak perturbation coupled to the transverse component of the pseudospin degrees of freedom, the temperature derivative of an observable conjugate to such a weak perturbing force is highly sensitive to the ring-exchange energy scale. Using this scheme, it is shown that the difference between thermal expansion coefficients along the [100] and [010] directions should show a peak at the ring-exchange energy scale for non-Kramers QSI. Similarly, the temperature derivative of the magnetization, $dM/dT$, of dipolar-octupolar pyrochlores under a weak magnetic field can also detect the same signal. Moreover, the sign of these signatures distinguishes the zero-flux and $π$-flux QSI states.
summary: The paper introduces advanced thermodynamic spectroscopy techniques to overcome experimental difficulties in measuring the ring-exchange energy scale in Quantum Spin Ice. By analyzing how observables like thermal expansion and magnetization change with weak external fields, the authors propose clean diagnostic signatures that can distinguish between different magnetic flux states within QSI materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a reliable thermodynamic probe to detect the elusive ring-exchange energy scale in Quantum Spin Ice (QSI).
main_result: Novel probes, such as anisotropic thermal expansion ($\Delta \alpha$) for non-Kramers QSI and $dM/dT$ for dipolar-octupolar pyrochlores, are shown to be highly sensitive to this ring-exchange scale.
method: The authors use a novel thermodynamic approach involving coupling the system to weak perturbations (strain or magnetic fields) and analyzing the resulting temperature derivatives of observables ($\gamma_X$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on Quantum Spin Ice, modeled by the XXZ Hamiltonian on the pyrochlore lattice. The analysis distinguishes between non-Kramers and dipolar-octupolar variants to propose distinct experimental signatures.
key_observables: Difference in thermal expansion coefficients ($\Delta \alpha$), temperature derivative of magnetization ($dM/dT$), and the generalized response function $\gamma_X$.
important_parameters: Ring-exchange energy scale ($g$), zero-flux vs. $\pi$-flux state, weak perturbation strength ($\lambda$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions in the coupling constant ($\lambda$) and assumes that specific probes (like $\Delta \alpha$) are immune to direct nuclear Schottky anomalies.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate anisotropic thermal expansion spectroscopy showing how the measured signal tracks the lower energy anomaly of the specific heat, and diagrams show the microscopic dependence on flux sector for $dM/dT$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using perturbation theory to derive $\gamma_X$ from weak coupling. It then applies this formalism to two distinct experimental platforms (NK and DO pyrochlores) to predict measurable signatures distinguishing different QSI ground states.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, quantitative roadmap for interpreting complex thermodynamic measurements in frustrated quantum magnets, linking microscopic Hamiltonian parameters ($g$) directly to macroscopic, measurable responses ($\Delta \alpha$, $dM/dT$).
